Branches are often situated in residential areas such as this.]] '''Heron Foods Ltd.''' (formerly '''Heron Frozen Foods Ltd''' and '''Grindells Butchers Ltd''') is an English supermarket chain founded in 1979 and based in [[Speke]], England. As of October 2025, the company has 338 stores in Britain and primarily sells frozen food, but has a wide range of ambient and chilled stock with brands including [[Müller (company)|Müller]], [[Birds Eye]] and [[McCain Foods]], as well as several lines using the Heron Foods brand. The company has been owned by [[B & M|B&M]] since August 2017. ==History== [[File:Heron Foods - South Street - geograph.org.uk - 1853339.jpg|thumb|right|A branch showing the old logo.]] The company was first registered in October 1978 as Grindells Butchers.Companies House Information on Company 01392197 The first store was opened by the Grindell family on Holderness Road, [[Kingston upon Hull|Hull]] in 1979.{{cite web|url=http://www.heronfoods.com/About.aspx|title=About Heron Foods|access-date=5 January 2018|archive-date=24 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324145436/http://www.heronfoods.com/About.aspx|url-status=dead}} In 1981 the company changed name to Heron Frozen Foods. Shortly after Anthony Grindell sold the business to his sister and her family – the Heucks. In 1999 Heron Foods bought 17 [[Dawn Til Dusk]] convenience stores after that chain went into [[receivership]], bringing its total number of stores to over 100.Independent Retail News 2 July 1999 COSTCUTTER LINKED WITH DAWN TIL DUSK STORES BYLINE: Daniel Pearce SECTION: NEWS; p. 10 Malcolm and Sheila Heuck had a joint controlling interest in the company from the beginning, but in February 2003, having reached retirement age, they sold their stake to management; from that point, the company was run by their sons Andrew, David and Michael.{{cite web|url=http://www.newsandstar.co.uk/new-frozen-food-shop-to-open-1.333531?referrerPath=home/2.1962|title=News & Star - New frozen food shop to open|access-date=5 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202213139/http://www.newsandstar.co.uk/new-frozen-food-shop-to-open-1.333531?referrerPath=home%2F2.1962|archive-date=2 February 2014|url-status=dead}} In September 2012 Heron Foods agreed to buy the Cooltrader frozen foods business from [[Iceland (supermarket)|Iceland]]. The deal included 54 of the 58 shops and the depot and head office of Cooltrader.{{cite web|url=http://www.just-food.com/news/iceland-agrees-cooltrader-sale-to-heron-foods_id120376.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120908005136/http://www.just-food.com/news/iceland-agrees-cooltrader-sale-to-heron-foods_id120376.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 September 2012|title=UK: Iceland agrees Cooltrader sale to Heron Foods|date=4 September 2012|access-date=5 January 2018}} The acquired Cooltrader outlets were converted to the Heron Foods brand.Retail Week 3 September 2012 Monday Iceland appoints Paul Foley as international business director In August 2017, it was announced that Heron Foods had been sold to B&M for £152 million.{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-humber-40805474|title=Family-run Heron Foods taken over by B&M in £152m deal|date=2 August 2017|work=BBC News|publisher=BBC|access-date=3 August 2017|archive-date=14 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190714111145/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-humber-40805474|url-status=live}} A number of new branches have been opened under the new '''B&M Express''' facia.{{cite web|url=https://heronfoods.com/news/article/stores/heron-flies-south-opens-first-store-in-luton|title=Heron Flies South to Open First Store in Luton|date=19 February 2020|access-date=19 February 2020|archive-date=21 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200721155950/https://heronfoods.com/news/article/stores/heron-flies-south-opens-first-store-in-luton|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url=https://heronfoods.com/storelocator/eyJyZXN1bHRfcGFnZSI6InN0b3JlbG9jYXRvciIsImRpc3RhbmNlOmZyb20iOiI1MS44Nzg2NzA3fC0wLjQyMDAyNTUwMDAwMDA2NTIiLCJsb2NhdGlvbl9maWVsZCI6Imx1dG9uIn0|title=B&M Express - Marsh Farm (Heron Foods)|date=19 February 2020|access-date=19 February 2020}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} ==Operations== The company's head office is at [[Melton, East Riding of Yorkshire|Melton]] in the [[East Riding of Yorkshire]] and it has around 250 outlets which are mostly located throughout the [[North of England]] and [[Midlands (England)|the Midlands]]. Heron Foods has developed its business in selling frozen and convenience store goods at a discount, the majority of which are household brands.Nottingham Evening Post 21 August 2012 Tuesday Edition 1; National Edition Innes England in hunt for stores for growing chain of supermarkets SECTION: BUSINESS POST;BUSINESS; p. 15 Heron occupies nine former [[Woolworths (United Kingdom)|Woolworth's]] locations.The Daily Telegraph (London) 19 January 2012 Thursday Edition 2; National Edition Pound legacy of Woolworths sites BYLINE: Harry Wallop SECTION: BUSINESS; p. 3 ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== {{commonscat}} *[https://www.heronfoods.com Official website] {{UK supermarkets}} [[Category:Retail companies of the United Kingdom]] [[Category:Companies based in the East Riding of Yorkshire]] [[Category:Retail companies established in 1979]] [[Category:Supermarkets of the United Kingdom]] [[Category:1979 establishments in England]]
